Subject: Clarify evidence slice & timestamp normalization for SOC2 Type II window

Hi Ava / Acme team,

Quick question as we're preparing the evidence bundle for Acme's SOC 2 Type II review: the auditor requested log coverage for the audit period, but we want to clarify acceptable approaches so we don't over-collect. Two specific items: 

1) Timestamp normalization: Our platform stores mixed timestamps (service events in UTC, some customer-submitted metadata in local tz). For evidence, do you require logs normalized to UTC (ISO8601 Z) or is it acceptable to include original timestamps with a mapping file that indicates timezone per source?

2) Slice vs full-month: Acme's ingest volume is huge (multi-TB/month). Would a statistically justified contiguous sample (e.g., a 72-hour slice at month-end that captures peak + off-peak) be acceptable for operational control testing, or do you require full-month exports for all systems? If sampling is permitted, what documentation do you need to support representativeness?

I've attached a blank evidence_manifest_template.csv and a 2MB sample S3 access log (s3_access_log_sample_202706.gz) so you can see our format.

Also: is a bridge letter required if there are any minor gaps between the evidence slice and the full period? If so, could you share a bridge_letter_template.pdf we can adapt?

We'd like to compress this into a short deliverable this week and want to make sure we meet your expectations.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher

Hi Sean / Redwood team / Acme,

Thanks for the clear note and the sample files — helpful. Short answers up front: UTC-normalized timestamps are preferred and representative slices can be accepted when justified. More detail below.

1) Timestamp normalization: Please provide logs normalized to UTC (ISO8601 with Z) where possible. If you cannot re-emit all logs in UTC, include the original timestamp plus a sidecar mapping file that indicates the source's timezone and any DST rules used. For transparency, we prefer the primary timestamp column be UTC so our tooling can align events across systems.

2) Sampling / slice: We will accept a contiguous, statistically defensible slice for operational control testing instead of full-month exports in high-volume systems. Required items for sampling acceptance: 
  - Rationale for slice selection (e.g., contains both peak and off-peak windows, no one-off maintenance windows)
  - Evidence that the slice is contiguous and representative (traffic profiles, P95 latency, error rates for slice vs month)
  - A manifest mapping slice timestamps back to the full dataset (so we can confirm there are no systemic anomalies)
  - If controls are dependent on day boundaries (e.g., daily reconciliation), ensure the slice covers at least one reconciliation cycle boundary.

Bridge letter: If you have any unavoidable gaps between the sample and the full control population (for example, short retention/archival windows that drop raw logs within 7 days), a bridge letter is recommended. I've attached a simple bridge_letter_template.pdf and also uploaded a signed example we used previously to the secure upload link below.

Other notes: 
  - Please include SHA256 checksums for compressed artifacts in the manifest.
  - For S3 access logs, provide both the raw gz files and an extracted CSV sample showing parsed fields.
  - Leap seconds / clock skew: not a formal blocker — include notes in the manifest if any system applies leap-second corrections or NTP adjustments that could affect ordering.

Upload artifacts to: https://redwood-secure-upload.company/req/ACME-2027-evidence (we will confirm receipt).

Hope this helps — happy to jump on a short call if you'd prefer to walk through the mapping.

Best,

Thanks Ava — that's very helpful. Two quick follow-ups so we can prepare the package correctly: 

• For the UTC primary timestamp: is it acceptable to add a column utc_ts alongside existing_ts (i.e., do not replace original fields)? That would make our pipeline changes minimal.

• For the representative slice: we'd like to propose a 72-hour contiguous window that spans Fri 00:00 UTC -> Sun 23:59 UTC at the end of May (contains weekday peak and weekend traffic patterns). We'll attach a short sampling rationale doc showing traffic profiles and P95 latency comparisons. Is that contiguous 72-hour approach OK, or do you prefer a slice that includes a typical end-of-month reconciliation run (we can shift to include the MTD close if needed)?

We'll include SHA256 checksums in the manifest and a short note on NTP behavior. If bridge letter is recommended, we'll adapt the template you provided and forward that for your review.

If it's useful, we can set up a 30-minute screen-share with an engineer to walk through the manifest and the log structure before we upload.

Sean

Sean —

Yes to the utc_ts column approach (please keep original timestamps untouched). The 72-hour contiguous window is acceptable so long as your rationale shows it captures typical traffic and any daily reconciliation cycle if applicable. If you can include one slice that covers an MTD close, that's ideal; otherwise include a reconciliation cycle artifact separately.

Please: 
  - Add utc_ts column for every event row and keep original timestamp column.
  - Include a one-page statistical summary comparing slice vs month (P50, P90, P95, error rate) and a short note on any anomalies.
  - Provide SHA256 checksums in evidence_manifest_template.csv for each artifact.
  - If you plan to use a bridge letter, adapt the attached template and send it back to us for review — we'll add an auditor signature if acceptable.

I'll review the manifest once uploaded and quick-turn feedback where possible. If you want to schedule a 30-min call, Tuesday afternoon PST works for me.

Thanks — looking forward to the upload.

Ava
